Strongly Associated Pairs of Features

Source: R/assoc_pairs.r
assoc_pairs.Rd

Lists the pairs of features whose correlation is at least threshold in absolute value, and optionally significant, from a sparcc() or rho_p() result: one row per pair, strongest first.

Usage

assoc_pairs(x, threshold = 0.3, alpha = NULL, p_adjust = "BH")

Arguments

x

Correlations between features: a result of sparcc() or rho_p(), or a symmetric matrix of correlations with 1 on the diagonal (such as from stats::cor()).

threshold

Keep the pairs whose correlation is at least this in absolute value (\(|r| \ge\) threshold), both positive and negative ones. Default 0.3, the SparCC paper's cutoff for a network. 0 keeps every pair.

alpha

Also keep only the pairs whose adjusted p-value is at most this. NULL (the default) for no p-value filter. Needs p-values: a sparcc() result made with permutations.

p_adjust

How to adjust the p-values for testing every pair: one of stats::p.adjust.methods. Default 'BH' (Benjamini & Hochberg's false discovery rate). The adjustment is over all the pairs of x, not just those kept. Used only when x has p-values.

Value

A data frame of class c("ecodive_assoc_pairs", "data.frame"), one row per pair kept, ordered from the largest \(|r|\) to the smallest, with columns:

  • from, to: the two features' names (their positions, as text, when the features have no names), from being the one that comes first in the input table.

  • association: their correlation, with its sign.

  • p_value, p_adjusted: when x has p-values, the pair's p-value and its adjustment by p_adjust over all pairs.

Attributes: method (the method that made x, such as "sparcc"; absent for a matrix), threshold, and, when used, alpha and p_adjust.

With no pair kept, the data frame has no rows.

Details

Pairs whose correlation is NA or NaN are never kept. threshold and alpha both apply when both are given; use threshold = 0 to filter on p-values alone. The pairs kept are the edges of a correlation network with this cutoff.

Enough permutations. A permutation p-value is at least \(1 / (B + 1)\) for \(B\) null datasets, and adjusting it for testing every pair multiplies it by up to the number of pairs \(m\). So with too few permutations no pair can pass alpha, however strong. With Benjamini-Hochberg, \(k\) pairs at the smallest p-value pass only when \(m / (k (B + 1)) \le\) alpha: 20 features (190 pairs) and one strong pair need about 3,800.

Only correlations are accepted. vlr() and phi_s() are dissimilarities (smaller means more proportional), so "above a cutoff" doesn't apply to them: use rho_p(), their correlation-scale counterpart.

See also

sparcc(), rho_p(), stats::p.adjust().

Examples

    # 60 samples of 20 taxa, with five correlated pairs
    set.seed(1)
    basis <- matrix(rnorm(60 * 20), 60, 20)
    for (i in c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9))
      basis[, i + 1] <- basis[, i] + rnorm(60, sd = 0.5)
    counts <- matrix(
      rpois(1200, exp(basis + 4)), 60, 20,
      dimnames = list(NULL, paste0('OTU', 1:20)) )

    r <- sparcc(counts, n_draws = 20)
    assoc_pairs(r)
#> # A data.frame: 11 × 3
#> # SparCC Correlation: pairs with |r| >= 0.3
#>    from  to    association
#>    <chr> <chr>       <dbl>
#>  1 OTU5  OTU6        0.885
#>  2 OTU9  OTU10       0.883
#>  3 OTU7  OTU8        0.871
#>  4 OTU3  OTU4        0.837
#>  5 OTU1  OTU2        0.725
#>  6 OTU14 OTU18      -0.45
#>  7 OTU2  OTU16       0.38
#>  8 OTU11 OTU13       0.365
#>  9 OTU4  OTU20       0.362
#> 10 OTU14 OTU16       0.355
#> 11 OTU3  OTU20       0.339
#> # Attributes: method, threshold

    # Only the strongest
    assoc_pairs(r, threshold = 0.5)
#> # A data.frame: 5 × 3
#> # SparCC Correlation: pairs with |r| >= 0.5
#>   from  to    association
#>   <chr> <chr>       <dbl>
#> 1 OTU5  OTU6        0.885
#> 2 OTU9  OTU10       0.883
#> 3 OTU7  OTU8        0.871
#> 4 OTU3  OTU4        0.837
#> 5 OTU1  OTU2        0.725
#> # Attributes: method, threshold

    # Significant pairs, from 999 null datasets
    r <- sparcc(counts, n_draws = 10, permutations = 999)
    assoc_pairs(r, alpha = 0.05)
#> # A data.frame: 5 × 5
#> # SparCC Correlation: pairs with |r| >= 0.3 and BH-adjusted p <= 0.05
#>   from  to    association p_value p_adjusted
#>   <chr> <chr>       <dbl>   <dbl>      <dbl>
#> 1 OTU5  OTU6        0.893   0.001      0.038
#> 2 OTU9  OTU10       0.883   0.001      0.038
#> 3 OTU7  OTU8        0.874   0.001      0.038
#> 4 OTU3  OTU4        0.839   0.001      0.038
#> 5 OTU1  OTU2        0.729   0.001      0.038
#> # Attributes: method, threshold, alpha, p_adjust

    # Correlations from elsewhere
    assoc_pairs(cor(log(counts + 1)), threshold = 0.5)
#> # A data.frame: 5 × 3
#> # Correlations: pairs with |r| >= 0.5
#>   from  to    association
#>   <chr> <chr>       <dbl>
#> 1 OTU5  OTU6        0.915
#> 2 OTU9  OTU10       0.911
#> 3 OTU7  OTU8        0.888
#> 4 OTU3  OTU4        0.853
#> 5 OTU1  OTU2        0.767
#> # Attributes: threshold
